candidates.source_name: Portal javnih naročil (Uradni list RS) – pregled objav, filtrirano po CPV/ponudniku
candidates.why_relevant: Official Slovenian public-procurement publication portal. Its 'Pregled objav' view accepts URL query filters (e.g. ?f=ponudnik:<maticna>|datum:YYYY,M,D-|cpv:66) which allows building payments-specific watchlists by CPV branch (66 financial, 30 card/equipment, 72 IT services) and by supplier registration number — the mechanism to catch card-processing, ATM, HSM and instant-payment procurements that never carry a 'banking' label.
candidates.access_status: public, no login for notice browsing
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Scheduled HTTP GET of PregledObjav.aspx with pinned CPV/date/supplier query strings; parse notice list, then fetch each notice page. Keep polite rate limits.
candidates.discovered_via_method: sl-language search on CPV + portal name, then snowball from result URLs

candidates.source_name: Erar (KPK) – public-money transaction explorer
candidates.why_relevant: Discloses transactions of public bodies and state/municipality-owned companies by payee. Because it is payee-searchable, it reveals actual money flows to payments vendors (Bankart, card personalisation firms, ATM/HSM suppliers) even where no tender notice exists — effectively an award-notice substitute for below-threshold and utility spending.

negative_findings.description: Repeated sl-language searching for a Bankart procurement/supplier page ('razpis', 'javno naročilo', 'nabava', 'dobavitelji') returned only corporate, careers, settlement-document and registry pages. No evidence was found that Bankart d.o.o. publishes its own tenders or a supplier portal.
negative_findings.result_summary: Bankart appears to procure privately; its buying is visible only indirectly (press releases, job ads, scheme documents, counterparty announcements, Erar payee flows).
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The single highest-yield procurement node in this cell has no direct tender feed, so the collection design must lean on indirect and pointer sources rather than a notice crawler.

negative_findings.description: No named vendor-selection or contract award was found for the Flik / BIPS instant-payment build, in either sl or en searching.
negative_findings.result_summary: Sources confirm Bankart operates BIPS and TIPS connectivity and that all Slovenian PSPs agreed in 2018 to establish Flik, but no implementation contractor is publicly identified.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Instant-payment programme vendors must be inferred from job ads, conference speakers and vendor-side references; treat any vendor attribution as unverified until a primary document is found.

negative_findings.description: The only concrete Slovenian card-personalisation tender surfaced was the ZZZS health-insurance smart-card award to Cetis, reported by Delo on an old (c.2007) article now on the legacy old.delo.si domain.
negative_findings.result_summary: Evidence exists that a domestic personalisation tender market exists, but the retrieved instance is very old and non-banking.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Recency risk: do not treat this as current market structure; a targeted archive query against the procurement portal by CPV 30162*/22 is needed for live personalisation contracts.

negative_findings.description: The seed term 'procesni center' and the plain word 'razpis' are noisy: 'razpis' is used in Slovenia for job vacancies and training-course enrolments (e.g. ZBS course PDFs literally titled 'Razpis-Urnik-Placilni-promet'), and 'Bankart' also matches the unrelated orthopaedic Bankart lesion and Sarajevo/Bankart-like place names in English results.
negative_findings.result_summary: Precision loss on both sl and en sides of the query set.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Query design must pair 'razpis/javno naročilo' with procurement-specific companions ('naročnik', 'ponudnik', 'oddaja naročila', 'razpisna dokumentacija') and, in English, always with 'Slovenia payments' to avoid the medical homonym.

negative_findings.description: No dedicated Slovenian source was found for HSM, tokenisation or scheme-certification (Visa/Mastercard) procurement; searches in sl for 'kartična shema ... implementacija' returned only consumer FAQ and general-press scheme-competition coverage.
negative_findings.result_summary: This sub-topic of the cell currently has zero direct sources.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Certification and crypto-hardware buying cycles are a real Printec-relevant demand signal but are invisible in public SI sources; they will need vendor-side and conference sources instead.

coverage_gaps.description: Non-bank acquirers and PSPs operating in Slovenia (e.g. domestic Activa card system, foreign acquirers, e-money institutions notified to Banka Slovenije) were not individually enumerated in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Parse the Banka Slovenije register of notified payment/e-money institutions (PPS katalog PDF) into an actor table, then run per-actor sl queries for procurement and vendor announcements.

coverage_gaps.description: The procurement portal's filter syntax was observed but the payments-relevant CPV code set was not yet enumerated or validated against live results.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build and test an explicit CPV list (66 financial; 30162/30144 card and card-processing equipment; 48/72 software and IT services; 50 maintenance; 30123 ATM-adjacent) and pin it into both the enarocanje.si query strings and the TED API filter.

coverage_gaps.description: No archival source was established for notices that expire or are withdrawn from the portal, and no vendor-side reference/case-study channel (NCR/Atos/Worldline/Thales/IDEMIA/Diebold Slovenia references) was scouted.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add a web-archive snapshot step for every captured notice URL, and scout vendor press/reference pages plus their SI partner networks as an indirect award-notice substitute.

coverage_gaps.description: It was not established whether Bankart or the commercial banks fall under the Slovenian public-procurement act as utility/sectoral contracting entities, which determines whether any of their buying must be published at all.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Check ZJN-3 scope and the official list of contracting authorities/sectoral entities; if Bankart is out of scope, formally down-weight the notice-crawling strategy for this cell.

coverage_gaps.description: Local-language coverage was achieved for procurement, Flik, ATM and personalisation terms, but no Slovene terminology was located for tokenisation, HSM/key management or scheme certification procurement.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Harvest Slovene technical vocabulary from Bankart job ads, ZBS course syllabi and bank T&Cs (likely 'tokenizacija', 'varnostni modul', 'certificiranje kartične sheme') and re-run searches with the confirmed terms.

brief: Slovenia's payments procurement landscape is bifurcated: a well-structured public layer (Portal javnih naročil / e-JN / TED, plus Erar and OPSI for actual money flows) that captures state-linked buyers such as Banka Slovenije, SID banka and UJP, and an opaque private layer where the decisive actor — Bankart, the shared processor for most Slovenian banks — procures with no public tender feed at all. Because of that asymmetry, the highest-value tracking for this cell is indirect: Bankart press releases, Flik scheme and integration documentation, ZBS payment/card committee outputs and annual reports, bank ATM-network and merger announcements, issuer T&C version diffs, and payee-level searches in Erar keyed to Bankart's registration identifiers. Local-language terms are essential and partly counter-intuitive ('javno naročilo', 'naročnik/ponudnik', 'razpisna dokumentacija', 'bankomatska mreža', 'personalizacija kartic', 'takojšnja plačila'), while the bare word 'razpis' is heavily polluted by job and training notices and 'Bankart' collides with a medical term in English. Biggest open risks: no direct source yet for HSM/tokenisation/scheme-certification buying, and an unresolved legal question of whether Bankart or the commercial banks are sectoral contracting entities at all.
